findings.quote: Write the second law for each block, with its own sign for the direction it moves.
findings.problem: The lesson teaches three pulley rules (same-size accelerations over fixed pulleys, a separate sign for each object over a pulley, half the acceleration for a block on a movable pulley) and the shortcut now sends the student to a per-block method for any pulley. No example works a pulley case. Examples #3 and #4 cover a straight-line pair and a single hanging cable only. Two objects joined over a fixed pulley (an Atwood machine, or a block on a table pulled by a hanging block) is the standard application of tension in this lesson's goal, and the curriculum names ropes and pulleys as a context for Newton's-law problems. A student meets the sign rule in words only, and the round-1 failure shows what goes wrong without it: counting the two weights as the only outside forces gives 9.8 m/s^2 instead of 1.96 m/s^2 for 3 kg and 2 kg blocks. Writer rule 1 after round 1 names taught-but-not-worked cases as an L18 failure.
findings.source: Checklist L18; reader-rules.md L18 ruling (standard application of a skill in the lesson's goal); DepEd K to 12 SHS General Physics 1 curriculum guide, applications of Newton's laws to single-body and multibody dynamics: solve problems using Newton's laws in contexts such as, but not limited to, ropes and pulleys (curriculum class; see the dost-sei-L100 and upcat-L162 rows in the brief)
